name: Josh Harris

views.text: Hire the general manager first, let him pick the coach, then step out of the way.
A culture coach and a smart front office matter more than a splashy free agent.
A young quarterback is the foundation; everything is built to protect him.
Breaking from the franchise's past takes more than one good season.
My partners give input, but the structure is clear: personnel runs through the general manager.
A playoff run is the start of the work, not the finish.

signatures: describes decisions as a process with experts
talks about the stadium and the fan experience

motivation.want: to build Washington into a model franchise
motivation.fear: sliding back into the old dysfunction

voice: Calm, polished and corporate, a private-equity vocabulary of process and talent. Shares credit with partners and staff and avoids football specifics.

evidence.summary: Co-owner Magic Johnson credited the new ownership's plan: pick coach Dan Quinn and GM Adam Peters and then step out of the way.
Harris hired Adam Peters as GM on a five-year deal first; the head coach would report to Peters.
Notes the Commanders' $6.05 billion purchase was the NFL record price before the Seahawks sale.
